findings.evidence: | Specific commit | `git show <sha>`; for a merge commit, `git show --first-parent <sha>` |
findings.fix: Cut the command rows the model already knows (`git show <sha>`, `git diff`, `git diff --cached`) down to the parts it would get wrong: the merge-commit `--first-parent` form, `??` paths and the three-dot base diff. That keeps the table to non-obvious choices.

Add a short heuristic for telling causal changes from incidental ones before ranking. For example: "ignore formatting, lockfile and generated hunks; a candidate is a hunk whose removal would change behavior or a test outcome". This turns step 1 into a method rather than a declaration.

findings.evidence: For a diff over 500 lines, read `--stat` first, then the high-signal hunks.
findings.fix: Add a Git gotcha: lockfiles, snapshots and generated output often make up most of a large diff's lines and `--stat` ranks them first. Exclude them with pathspecs (for example `git diff <base>...HEAD -- . ':!*.lock' ':!package-lock.json'`) before choosing high-signal hunks.

findings.evidence: description: "Use when users ask what they learned, want an engineering takeaway, or reflect on recent commits, a branch diff, a specific commit, or staged/unstaged changes—even without naming Git or a principle. ... Not for generic engineering tutorials, ordinary bug reviews, or implementing refactors."
findings.fix: Use when users ask what they learned, want an engineering takeaway or retrospective insight, or reflect on a finished PR, feature branch, refactor, debugging session, recent commits, a specific commit or staged, unstaged or untracked changes, even without naming Git or a software engineering principle. Grounds one lesson in the actual diff, with evidence and a next-time practice. Not for generic engineering tutorials, bug reviews, commit messages, release notes, postmortems or planning a refactor.

findings.evidence: Always read [the diff-signal lookup](references/se-principles.md); its evidence column is the check a principle name must pass.
findings.fix: Gate the lookup on scope: "Read references/se-principles.md at step 5 of Select and verify, once change evidence exists. Do NOT load it when nothing is in scope." That way, no-change runs and quick questions without a diff do not spend context on it.

findings.evidence: Every eval supplies a pasted diff, log or status file; none exercises the scope table (base resolution via `git symbolic-ref`, the merge-commit `--first-parent` case or the default feature-branch scope)
findings.fix: Add an eval with a fixture repo, or a pasted `git log --graph` and status, for a feature branch off origin/main that contains a merge commit. Assert that the answer states the base it used and reads the merge with `--first-parent`. Also add a should-trigger query that names neither Git nor 'lesson' (for example 'that took way longer than it should have, anything I should do differently on the next ticket?').

findings.evidence: Then `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` and `git diff <base>...HEAD`. ... If nothing is in scope, say there is no change evidence and stop
findings.fix: Add a branch for a feature branch already merged into the base (the 'PR #217 just merged' case): when `<base>..HEAD` is empty but the branch has its own commits, find the merge with `git log --merges --first-parent <base> --grep=<branch>` or use `git reflog`/the PR's merge commit, and read it with `git show --first-parent <merge>`. Without this branch the skill stops with 'no change evidence' when the work is actually present.

findings.evidence: 'NEVER cite a file, commit or line you did not read' restates baseline evidence hygiene; 'List the candidate causal changes' at line 39 likewise adds generic process rather than the specific scope and false-positive knowledge that distinguishes this skill.
findings.fix: Compress selection steps 1–3 into one instruction to rank causal changes by demonstrated consequence and defensible counterfactual. Fold source-location recording into verification step 4 instead of keeping the standalone generic citation reminder.

findings.evidence: 'git show <merge> prints a combined diff that is empty for a clean merge' is too absolute: a conflict-free merge can have a nonempty combined diff when a file changed relative to both parents.
findings.fix: Replace the explanation with: 'Combined diffs show only files changed relative to every parent, so they can omit changes introduced by a merge, including clean merges. Use git show --first-parent <sha> to inspect what entered the first-parent branch.' Keep the existing first-parent command.

findings.evidence: The six cases include 'extraction-adds-coupling', 'mechanical-rename', 'precise-range' and 'untracked-only', but no assertions verify base resolution, dirty-base scope selection or first-parent merge evidence. Supplied diffs and logs bypass most of the Git evidence-selection workflow.
findings.fix: Add reproducible repository-backed eval cases for feature-branch base selection, a dirty base branch and a merge commit. Assert the selected scope, inclusion or exclusion of working changes, and the changes introduced relative to the merge's first parent.

findings.evidence: 'git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD; if that fails, local main or master' does not handle a dangling origin/HEAD: symbolic-ref can return a branch name whose target does not exist, after which log and diff fail without reaching the documented fallback.
findings.fix: Validate each candidate base with git rev-parse --verify --quiet "<base>^{commit}" before using it. If the remote default does not resolve to a commit, try local main, then master, then the existing last-five-commits fallback, and state which scope was selected.
